summary: CLI agent exposes host to remote command execution via vendor WebSocket/AppSync channel
details: When the operator starts the CLI (`ai-support-agent start`), it opens a persistent WebSocket to api.ai-support-agent.com at /ws/agent-terminal and subscribes to an AppSync notification channel from the same vendor API. Inbound 'stdin' frames are base64-decoded and written directly into a node-pty session (handleStdin → session.write(Buffer.from(msg.data,'base64'))); inbound 'tmux_list_sessions' / 'tmux_kill_session' / 'split_pane' messages are turned into execFile('tmux',...) calls using session names supplied over the network. Separately, AppSync 'agent-command' notifications are fetched via deps.client.getCommand(commandId) and dispatched through executeCommand(detail.type, trustedPayload,...) into local handlers that include chat/tool-use, setup, reboot, update, sync_repository, ssh_exec, and server_setup_exec. Whoever controls api.ai-support-agent.com can drive an interactive shell and invoke arbitrary command handlers on the host running the CLI. The darwin-service and linux-service modules install this agent as a persistent user/system service and modify PATH so the channel is available across sessions. This is the package's advertised function — a remote-driven support agent — and the destination is the vendor's own API, but the resulting capability is full-host remote code execution on the operator's machine gated only by the vendor's server-side auth.
